structuralFindings: Entire property is 8 PRIVATE VILLAS, beachfront — priced as PACKAGES (Couples/Family/Owners Villa), not per-person or per-standard-room. This is a fundamentally different pricing unit from every other property in this batch.
'All Packages are at a set rate' — single occupancy is treated (and priced) as a full Couples Package, i.e. no single-occupancy discount exists.
Family Package price is split into two figures ('3 OR 4 PAX Respectively') — a single flat rate for 3 pax and a separate flat rate for 4 pax, not a per-person rate.
Owners Villa is an 8-pax unit, its own flat package rate.

TWO seasons only: Standard (10 Jan - 19 Dec, EXCLUDING Easter week) and Peak (20 Dec - 9 Jan, INCLUDING Easter week) — note Easter week is carved OUT of the standard season and priced at Peak rates specifically, a distinct mechanic from every other property (which typically prices Easter as its own separate mini-season at an intermediate rate).

FOUR parallel rate tables exist in this single document: KES Rack (Resident), KES Nett (Resident), USD Rack (International/Non-Resident), USD Nett (International/Non-Resident). All four captured below since they're all short and clearly laid out.

USD Nett Peak Bed & Breakfast Couples Package figure reads as $245 in the extracted text — this is LOWER than the same package's Standard-season Nett BB rate of $322, which is internally inconsistent (Peak should not undercut Standard). Flagged as [Unverified — likely a source transcription/typo error, not corrected here] rather than silently adjusted; the equivalent Rack figures ($395 Peak vs $370 Standard) DO follow the expected Peak > Standard pattern, reinforcing that the $245 Nett figure looks like an error in the source, not a genuine discount.

Owners Villa USD Nett Peak BB figure is printed as '1.194' (period instead of comma) in the source — read as 1,194, consistent with the surrounding number formatting, but noted since it's a raw OCR/typesetting oddity in the original.

Nett rate tables carry an explicit anti-discounting instruction: 'Please do not share a discount over 5% off the rack rates, for industry fairness' — a resale-price constraint on whoever books this rate, worth remembering if this is used as a wholesale cost basis for a client-facing markup.

Child pricing is a flat KES/USD figure for ages 3-6 (not a percentage), while ages 7-11 get a 20% discount off the PER PERSON rate — but since packages are priced flat rather than per-person, how the 7-11 discount actually applies within a flat package price is not fully spelled out — flag as an open question if a 7-11-year-old is part of a booking.
Villa inventory: 7 of the 8 villas are 2-Bedroom (max 4 persons each); 1 villa is a 4-Bedroom (max 8 persons, presumably the 'Owners Villa').
